content.text: After some digging, it looks like the problem is that the metadata backup contains duplicate entries that all look like this:

{ "metadata" : { "id" : "87a0a8c317f1e7jcr:system/mode:metadata" } , "content" : { "key" : "87a0a8c317f1e7jcr:system/mode:metadata" , "properties" : { "" : { "workspaces" : [ "default" ] , "accessControl" : false } } } }
Removing the duplicate entry is not hard to do with a text editor, and I've created a prototype of a Java utility to automate this process:
.  After removing the duplicate entry, I've been able to restore backups successfully.
Ultimately, we will want to rely on import/export functionality that is based on the Fedora RESTful API, transacting in RDF and binaries.
However, if the current /fcr:backup and /fcr:restore endpoints work (with the help of your "BackupFixer"), it may be a way to get the community to ModeShape5 sooner.
At this point, we just need more testing.
Can you describe the size of the repository that your migrated?
Did your repository contain both binaries and objects?
, would you be able to test this (recognizing that it is not your preferred migration approach)?
I created sample content using the
script, which uses the same TTL file I added to the JMeter testing (
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-jmeter/blob/master/sample.ttl)

to create PCDM objects with attached files (100 MB each, I used actual TIFFs we are staging for ingest, or randomly-generated files when testing locally).  I tried a range of sizes, with the largest being 200GB of randomly-generated files.
I performed a basic test migration on an extremely small repository (305M backup directory with 147 files) without issue.
or
: would one of you be willing to create an executable jar out of BackupFixer.java for us to distribute to anyone else who runs into this issue?
Once that is done, I think we can close this ticket.
Alright, I attached a jar.
We should warn people that it's destructive (but likely not in a bad way), and should be run against a copy of the backup if the backup is irreplaceable.
see:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils/pull/12
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils/commit/ff42ba3f459a368fb48abbaabb45e444a66a5b39
Related issue:
https://issues.jboss.org/browse/MODE-2611
When restoring a backup from a 4.5.1 repository, I often see this error and the restore fails:
ERROR 08:42:50.311 (FedoraRepositoryRestore) Problems restoring up the repository:

java.sql.BatchUpdateException: Batch entry 615 INSERT INTO MODESHAPE_REPOSITORY (ID, CONTENT) VALUES ('87a0a8c317f1e7jcr:system/mode:metadata', ?) was aborted.  Call getNextException to see the cause.

comments.body:
After some digging, it looks like the problem is that the metadata backup contains duplicate entries that all look like this:

{ "metadata" : { "id" : "87a0a8c317f1e7jcr:system/mode:metadata" } , "content" : { "key" : "87a0a8c317f1e7jcr:system/mode:metadata" , "properties" : { "" : { "workspaces" : [ "default" ] , "accessControl" : false } } } }

Removing the duplicate entry is not hard to do with a text editor, and I've created a prototype of a Java utility to automate this process: BackupFixer.java . After removing the duplicate entry, I've been able to restore backups successfully.

Ultimately, we will want to rely on import/export functionality that is based on the Fedora RESTful API, transacting in RDF and binaries.
However, if the current /fcr:backup and /fcr:restore endpoints work (with the help of your "BackupFixer"), it may be a way to get the community to ModeShape5 sooner.

At this point, we just need more testing.

  • Can you describe the size of the repository that your migrated?
  • Did your repository contain both binaries and objects?
  • David Chandek-Stark (old account), would you be able to test this (recognizing that it is not your preferred migration approach)?

I created sample content using the pop.sh script, which uses the same TTL file I added to the JMeter testing (https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-jmeter/blob/master/sample.ttl) to create PCDM objects with attached files (100 MB each, I used actual TIFFs we are staging for ingest, or randomly-generated files when testing locally). I tried a range of sizes, with the largest being 200GB of randomly-generated files.
I performed a basic test migration on an extremely small repository (305M backup directory with 147 files) without issue.

Esmé Cowles or Michael Durbin: would one of you be willing to create an executable jar out of BackupFixer.java for us to distribute to anyone else who runs into this issue?
Once that is done, I think we can close this ticket.
Alright, I attached a jar. backup-fixer.jar We should warn people that it's destructive (but likely not in a bad way), and should be run against a copy of the backup if the backup is irreplaceable.
Michael Durbin Esmé Cowles see: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils/pull/12
